analysis.title: GS Basics: Rotational Market. Semi Indigestion. Bond Vol Compression.
key_insights: Asia saw a sharply rotational session: KOSPI fell 5-6%, Nikkei 1.5-2%, Taiwan 2%, with CXMT news hitting memory stocks. Samsung and Hynix fell 7-10%, and Kioxia, Advantest, Tokyo Electron and SoftBank were also under pressure.
In Japan, five stocks account for essentially the entire Nikkei decline, and TOPIX is trading slightly up. The author reads this as an unwind of crowded positions, not indiscriminate selling.
CXMT is described as a legitimate long-term concern for memory economics.

Microsoft's Maia 300 custom chips are moving to TSMC's 2nm process. The author calls this incrementally negative for merchant GPU suppliers (NVDA) and positive for the custom silicon supply chain and aggregate compute consumption.

Hock Tan's comments comparing AI investors to gamblers were taken out of context. Broadcom and Intel both reaffirmed strong demand for another 2-3 years, potentially through 2030. Tan sees compute demand exceeding supply and said frontier labs with substantial revenue can afford expensive financing.

Meta's Muse Wonder and Wonder Full look competitive at the frontier, potentially adding another serious player alongside OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. The author notes some questions around benchmarking. Prediction markets anticipate another major Google release soon.

The author's view is that frontier competition requires more compute, so aggregate compute demand is not bearish even if the economics shift around the supply chain. The legitimate concerns are the ability to complete capacity and deliver power, which is driving further de-rating in the capex vertical.

The market had become very long one corner and short everything else. SPX barely moved yesterday while semis underperformed and the broader market strengthened. Dispersion has flipped, with equal weight and the Russell outperforming, bonds stabilizing, bond vol compressing and gold finding a bid.
Last week was difficult for alpha. Managers with strong years are incentivized to protect them, which reduces appetite to intermediate risk and makes crowded positioning produce violent rotations.
The Russia/Ukraine energy ceasefire did not hold. Trump announced a deal that surprised Kyiv and was not confirmed by Moscow, and Russia struck Ukrainian power infrastructure within hours.

Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport exposed Saudi air defence vulnerabilities, yet Brent is lower and production is intact. The market is separating geopolitical escalation from barrels actually lost, which the author calls a fragile equilibrium.
Bonds are stabilizing: yields appear to have found a level and implied vol has given back nearly half its move.
Oil is unresolved. If energy takes out its highs with velocity, markets would struggle in a much more correlated fashion.
Aggregate equity exposure remains very low and nets are conservative. The author calls this rotation, not wholesale liquidation, and expects a choppy market while positioning clears.

The author expects Russell, equal weight and Europe to outperform while AI hardware digests its excesses. Hyperscalers are not expected to fall much because they own scarce compute, and the hardware leg is seen as a dip that gets bought.
Financials could reinforce the rotation, with a low bar given de-rating ahead of earnings.
Watch list: Waller and Barkin speaking, bank earnings, SEMICON West headlines on capex, packaging and HBM, ASML tomorrow and TSMC Thursday.
